relations: Fingertip contact with the bubble's base holds it in place until pressure or slip breaks the film.
A slight finger movement or air current deforms the spherical bubble and shifts its iridescent reflections.
If the film ruptures at the contact point, the bubble bursts into droplets and mist.
Buoyancy lifts the bubble off the finger once contact weakens, letting it drift upward.
